Data handling

Source: DATA_HANDLING.md

tidycreel is a public R package. It ships no personal data. The only real survey records it ships are the de-identified Calamus 2016 fixtures below; every other dataset is synthetic or aggregate.

What this repository contains

Data Location Contains PII? Notes
Package datasets tracked data/*.rda (listed in .gitignore) no Synthetic or aggregate examples built by data-raw/ scripts
Calamus 2016 fixtures inst/calamus-2016/*.csv no Interview- and count-level survey records with no angler identifiers; shipped on purpose for validation
Absent-zero guard baseline scripts/absent-zero-guard-baseline.tsv no Code-location baseline for a CI check

What stays outside this repository

  • Agency survey data, interview records, permit or licence data, and any dataset with angler names, contact details or licence numbers. These live in private analysis repositories or on the agency’s own systems, never here.
  • Agency-specific field-name profiles: local files that are never committed (column maps for creel_schema() here; API field maps and YAML connection profiles in tidycreel.connect).
  • External validation data and the scripts that read it.

Credentials

  • Never written in code, tests, vignettes or examples. Read from the OS keyring (keyring::key_get()) or an environment file outside the repo.
  • Use read-only database and API accounts for analysis.
  • A credential that appears in a commit, log, issue or chat transcript is treated as compromised and rotated.

Safeguards

  • .gitignore is deny-by-default for data formats, archives and credential files. The files listed above are whitelisted by exact path; a new data file needs a deliberate git add -f and a new whitelist line after review.
  • .pre-commit-config.yaml runs gitleaks on staged changes; run pre-commit install once per clone to enable it. The maintainer’s working copy also runs a local staged-file PII audit that blocks identifier columns; that audit is not tracked.
  • Code that will touch identified data is developed and tested against synthetic data.

If something leaks

Treat the repository as public: a leaked file or secret has been exposed even if it is removed later. Back up, rewrite history in a throwaway clone, verify with count-only checks, force-push with explicit approval, ask GitHub to purge cached views, realign local clones, and rotate any exposed credential.
